svg.aria-label: Raspberry Pi 5 box: the Pi on layer 1 and a 60 by 80 mm perfboard on 18 to 20 mm columns carrying the HCW-P715 5 V 5 A buck, INA226 number 2 and the MCP2515 CAN module with level shifting of SO and INT; camera on CSI, INMP441 on I2S, four PG7 glands, in its own 170 by 120 by 55 box
svg.text: Fig. 11 — Raspberry Pi 5 box (Part 5A; SCHEMATIC S5): own box, own 5 V, platform CAN only
Placement: left crash bar (f), rear rack (e) or beside the Main Box on a plate (d). The platform bus has no stub limit, so the Pi may sit far from the DLC.

g.text: Power: +12V_PROT (Board A, own fuse) → HCW-P715 → +5V_PI → Pi 5 V (GPIO 2/4); INA226 #2 on +5V_PI, Pi I2C 0x40.
The Pi is never powered from the LM2596. Current and brown-out behaviour on cold crank: measure (T0).
Platform CAN (can1): MCP2515 SI/SCK/CS ← GPIO10/11/8 (SPI0); SO → GPIO9 and INT → GPIO25
both level-shifted 5 V → 3.3 V (divider 1k/2k, or 74LVC1T45, or 3.3 V mod; CONFIRM per module). J1 120 Ω only at the bus end.
Vehicle CAN (can0, optional): listen-only tap for raw logging; `vehicle-linux-node-can` sets CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY; never TX.
Camera: Pi Camera Module 3 on CSI, 15→22-pin cable, front box (g) with lens window; LDW classic CV (§5b.5). Action-camera model: user.
Microphone: INMP441 I2S SCK GPIO18, WS GPIO19, SD GPIO20, L/R→GND (D-044; USB vs I2S still open).
Software: Kuksa databroker 0.7.1 + kuksa-can-provider (receive-only), black-box recorder, systemd units (linux-node#14).
Ferrites on the 12 V, CAN and camera cables outside the glands. Shielded camera lead if the run passes the engine.
• L3 live source Kuksa → vehicle-server (D-077 leaves MQTT/Zenoh/HTTP open; Claude recommends MQTT) · L2 node-health panel needs Q-016 per-node signal names (defs#159, user).
• Thermal and power budget of the Pi 5 in a sealed box in summer (hardware-architecture §5b.8): measure CPU temperature on the desk in the closed box before the first ride.
• Safe shutdown on ignition off (supercap/UPS or journal-safe mounts): not decided; the black-box recorder closes files on the trigger today.
